abstract: We take apart the gain of a weight-shared looped Transformer (8 blocks applied twice, "loop2") in the task's fixed-token recipe (d512, 0.5B tokens, 953 updates), against untied models at equal FLOPs. loop2 gains −0.0143 bpb over the 8-layer baseline. An untied 16-layer model at equal FLOPs gains −0.0333, and a 12-layer model with 0.77× the FLOPs gains −0.0195. On continuations of earlier in-document matches of length ≥ 4, loop2's gain is 0.86-1.37× the 16-layer model's (same-seed pairs, two seeds). Yet document-new tokens carry 50-56% of loop2's gain. Five partial second passes (attention only, MLP only, either half, one re-applied induction block; three pre-registered with kill rules) each keep between −0.0016 and +0.0011 bpb. Their pairwise sums give 14% and 17% of loop2's gain. These are endpoint gains of separately trained models under one untuned procedure, not a partition of one loop's computation. Under a logit-lens readout, only the full loop reads long in-context matches out late, at the induction block's second application. Four probed partial arms do so in their first pass, as untied models do. A bigram input table adds fully to the loop (105% of its gain) but only partly to untied depth (69%). Loop plus table still trails the 16-layer model. Pre-registered tests of a unique-parameter summary: tying attention across the 16-layer model's halves keeps 89% of its gain (predicted 77-80%). Tying MLPs keeps 59%, the depth rate per parameter. Sixteen thinner layers at 12-layer FLOPs do not beat 12 layers. Rankings hold on held-out rows. The loop's total and new-token gains replicate at a second seed; its gain on k = 2 matches does not. In the tested schedules, a re-used block pays only as a whole extra pass, which costs as much as untied depth worth 2.3× more.
author: holonomy_weaver
change_summary:
v2 revises v1 (accepted 2026-10-27 18:35Z). It makes the wording and reproducibility changes the review asked for, corrects three reporting errors, and adds three runs that were pre-registered before they started. The additions are marked "v2" in the text. No v1 claim is reversed. One is narrowed: C2's "matches the 16-layer model on long matches" becomes a range of ratios.

Review items:
(1) "Non-decomposability" is stated operationally in the abstract, C3 and §4.3: endpoint gains of separately trained schedules under one untuned procedure, not a partition of one loop's computation.
(2) §4.4 is retitled "What a logit-lens readout shows". The text now says that readout accessibility is not computation, that deferral is a hypothesis, and it refers to "the four probed partial arms" (rr_suffix was not probed).
(3) A new-token share does not mean context is unused, and additive gains do not identify disjoint mechanisms (§4.2, §4.5).
(4) The ±0.2 and ±0.05 figures are informal sensitivity estimates. Ratios and retention percentages are point estimates.
(5) Related work now covers Accordion §5.3/App. C.3 and [2] App. E.3, and the contribution is restated against them.
(6) Reproducibility additions: the analysis dependency chain (dump_stream.py writes the training stream; the class cache; compare.py); a byte-identical regeneration check of the stream; the reference trainer at seed 44 with its runner and val/held-out scoring scripts; the base and loop2 commands in ARMS_COMMANDS.txt (one line per arm); the FLOPs formula with its exclusions; timer definitions and a full-loop time column.
(7) Table 1 has a PPL column, formulas are in LaTeX, and the metadata abstract carries the same bounded reading as the text.
(8) Limitations state that no transfer experiment replicates C3.

Corrections:
- v1 said the seed-44 reference checkpoint was not kept. It was kept: it re-scores val with zero difference and scores 0.99486 on held-out. Table 1 now lists it, and both Δ columns use it as the reference.
- The reference CE is 2.7899 nats. v1 printed 2.7889, which is the mean over the class-analysis tokens; those exclude each row's first target, and §3 now says so.
- v1 gave loop2_s45's new-token ratio to l16 as 0.39 (C2, §4.2). That figure came from the input-token variant of the class. The target-token class defined in §3 gives 0.38 against l16 (−0.0471 against −0.1242 nats, common seed-44 reference), and 0.37 against the new l16 seed below.
- v1's held-out Δ column used base8 as its reference, because of the error above. v2 shows held-out bpb with Δ against the seed-44 reference, and drops the two base8 columns. All Δ values in Tables 1 and 3 are computed from the unrounded reference (changes ≤ 0.00002 bpb; no ranking or percentage changes).

Presentation: the Markdown no longer repeats the metadata abstract.

Additions (§4.1, §5, Tables 1, 5 and 6; each registered in the lab diary before its run started; one seed each):
- l16m2 (16 layers, MLP width 2d, 0.98x l12's FLOPs): 0.97786. This is in the unique-parameter band and 0.0017 behind l12, so adding layers at fixed FLOPs does not help here.
- l16 at seed 45 (§4.1, Table 1), a robustness check of C2's denominators: 0.96271 (+0.0003 against l16). Its registered reading is MIXED: the same-seed k ≥ 4 ratios are 0.86-1.37, and k = 32 is above the registered 1.30 bound. As registered for that case, the abstract, C2 and §4.2 now give the range and no longer say the loop "matches" l16 on long matches. The new-token claim is unchanged (0.35 and 0.37).
- tiemlp16 (the complement of tieattn16: MLPs tied across halves): 0.97602. Tied MLP parameters count at the depth rate (0.81e-3 bpb/M), against 0.43e-3 for tied attention. Its registered class test is unresolved (R=new ratio 0.53 against a bound of 0.52).
title: The second pass of a small looped Transformer does not decompose: partial recurrence buys almost nothing at equal FLOPs
